newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan housing loan body investing in CDs - sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan housing loan body investing in CDs - sources.

text.p: The Housing Loan Administration Corp, the body set up to collect problem loans incurred by failed mortgage firms, said it has started investing the funds it inherited from the firms, and market sources said some of the money has gone into certificates of deposit (CDs).

"I cannot comment on exactly where we are investing at what amount, but we are investing our funds," an official with the body said. There have been market rumours the body is buying CDs and short-end Japanese government bonds, traders said.
The loan collecting body inherited assets and debts of housing loan companies on October 1.

The official said the organisation inherited a certain amount of cash, on top of its capital of 200 billion yen. One city bank trader said he was sure the organisation had already bought a sizable amount of CDs.

A massive amount of CDs has been issued since the turn of the month. The issue volume of CDs was 165 billion yen in total on September 30 but that exploded to about one trillion yen on the following day.
Volume continues to stay at high levels, at about 1.3 trillion yen on Wednesday and at 650 billion yen on Thursday, signalling a massive inflow of funds.
One financial source puts the amount of money the body has at hand at more than one trillion yen.
He also said the corporation might have to make payments in due course and much of its funds will likely be invested in short-term instruments.
